name: Substitute Terms for Vows (Yad and Kinuyim)
notes: Covers the substitute and analogous terms (konam, konaḥ, konas, etc.) that function as valid vow formulations, and intimations of vows (yad l'nedarim)

name: Vows of Exhortation (Nidrei Zeiruzin)
notes: Vows used to encourage or pressure another in bargaining or social interaction, which the Sages dissolved without requiring a halakhic authority

name: Vows of Exaggeration (Nidrei Guzma)
notes: Hyperbolic vow expressions not intended literally, dissolved by the Sages without requiring a request to a halakhic authority

name: Unintentional Vows (Nidrei Shegagot)
notes: Vows taken under mistaken assumptions or forgotten circumstances, which the Sages dissolved without a formal request to a halakhic authority

name: Vows Impeded by Circumstances Beyond One's Control (Nidrei Ones)
notes: Vows that could not be fulfilled due to unforeseen circumstances (illness, flood, etc.) which are not binding

name: Dissolution of Vows by Halakhic Authority (Hatarat Nedarim — Process)
notes: The procedural mechanism by which a sage dissolves a vow, including the 'opening' (petach) — finding an extenuating circumstance — and regret (charatah); covers what types of openings are valid

name: Prohibition of Benefit by Vow (Hadarah/Muddar Hana'ah)
notes: The specific category of vow prohibiting one person from deriving benefit from another, covering what transactions, entry, lending, and assistance are included or excluded

name: Interpretation of Unspecified Vows (Stam Nedarim)
notes: Rules for determining the scope of vows when the vow term is unspecified — whether it follows common usage, regional custom, or the speaker's intent; includes lenient treatment of specified intent

name: Scope of Food Vows (What Foods are Included)
notes: Detailed rules for which foods and derivatives are included when one vows against a food type (wine includes/excludes vinegar, olive includes/excludes oil, etc.)

name: Partially Dissolved Vow is Entirely Dissolved
notes: The principle, attributed to Rabbi Akiva, that if part of a vow is dissolved it is entirely dissolved; covers interconnected vs. separate vow formulations

name: Time Limits in Vows
notes: Rules governing vows with specified time limits — 'today,' 'this week,' 'this month,' 'until Passover,' 'until the rains' — including whether 'until' means before or at the end of the event

name: Husband's Nullification of Wife's Vows
hebrew: הפרת נדרי האשה על ידי הבעל
notes: Detailed laws of when and how a husband can nullify his wife's vows, including timing (same day), which vows qualify (affliction, affecting relations), betrothed vs. married, and joint nullification by father and husband

name: Father's Authority over Betrothed Daughter's Vows
notes: The joint authority of father and betrothed husband over the vows of a betrothed young woman, including what happens when one of them dies, and the limits of each one's authority

name: Yavam's Authority over Yevama's Vows
notes: Dispute among Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehoshua, and Rabbi Akiva whether a yavam can nullify the vows of his yevama while she awaits levirate marriage

name: Pre-emptive Nullification of Future Vows
notes: The question of whether a husband can preemptively nullify all future vows his wife will take; debate between Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis; includes the practice of Torah scholars before marriage

name: Vows of Affliction (Inui Nefesh)
notes: The category of vows a husband can nullify because they cause affliction to the wife — definition and scope of what constitutes inui nefesh vs. what does not

name: Vows Affecting Relations Between Husband and Wife
notes: The category of vows a husband can nullify because they affect their marital relationship — including vows about work obligations, sexual prohibition, and similar matters

name: False Vows to Protect Life or Property from Murderers and Robbers
notes: The permission to make false vow-like declarations to protect oneself or one's property from robbers and tax collectors; dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel on scope

name: Shared Property and Vows of Benefit
notes: How vows of benefit prohibition operate when partners share a courtyard or other property; whether each can enter their own portion; forced sale of portion to avoid causing transgression

name: Validity of Gift as Means of Circumventing a Vow
notes: The rule that a gift given solely to circumvent a vow must be a genuine gift capable of being consecrated; the Beit Horon incident; transferring property to a third party to feed someone bound by a vow

name: Interpretation of Vow Language According to Common Usage
notes: The principle that vow language is interpreted according to the common usage of the speaker and their locale — covering terms like 'seafarers,' 'those with dark heads,' 'those who rest on Shabbat,' etc.

name: Vow by Association with Forbidden or Sacred Object
hebrew: נדר הבא מכוח קדשים או איסורים
notes: The rule that a vow takes effect only when the object of association is itself forbidden by vow (e.g., korban), not by Torah law (e.g., pig, neveilah); includes the hierarchy of valid vow associations

name: Vow Within a Vow (Neder b'Neder)
notes: The rule that an additional vow can stack onto an existing vow prohibition, unlike oaths which cannot stack (ein shevuah chal al shevuah)

name: Differences Between Vows and Oaths (Nedarim vs. Shevuot)
hebrew: חומרי נדרים על שבועות וחומרי שבועות על נדרים
notes: The comparative stringencies and leniencies of vows vs. oaths — vows apply to objects (devar sheyesh bo mamash) but not actions; oaths apply to actions but cannot override mitzvot; vow within vow vs. no oath within oath

name: Vow of Woman Removing Herself from All Jews
notes: The case of a woman who vows to be removed from all Jews sexually; the husband nullifies his portion and she remains forbidden to all others; the evolution of this halakha to prevent women from exploiting vows

name: Greatness of Circumcision (Gedulat haMilah)
notes: Aggadic and halakhic enumerations of the greatness of circumcision — overrides Shabbat, overrides tzaraat, 13 covenants, Moses punished for delay, Abraham called wholehearted only after circumcision
